sentences.text:
The instant appeal has been filed by the appellant- Insurance Company under the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 wherein award dated 30.06.2015 (for short the impugned award) passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Udhampur (for short the Tribunal) in claim petition titled as "Vinod Raggu Vs Jatin Gullati and Ors." is being challenged.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
02. The facts emerging from the record reveal that the respondent 1 herein preferred a claim petition before the Tribunal claiming compensation therein in respect of death of his father, namely,
Nath Ji Raggu having died on 17.11.2011 at Kallar Dhar Road, Udhampur in the vehicular accident caused by the Maruti Swift Car owned by respondent 2 herein and driven rashly and negligently by respondent 3 herein.
03.

The Tribunal after entertaining the claim petition and summoning the respondents in the claim petition being the appellant herein and respondents 2 and 3 herein framed following four issues on the pleadings of the parties after response came to be filed to the claim petition:
1. Whether the deceased Nath Ji Raggu died in the road traffic accident which was caused on 17.11.2011 by respondent No. 1 driver on account of the rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle No. JK14A-9497 (Swift Car)?
OPP 2.
If issue No. 1 is proved in affirmative, whether petitioner is entitled to compensation, if so to what effect?
OPP 3.

Whether the driver was driving the offending vehicle in violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy and the driver of offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident, if so to what effect?
OPR3 4. Relief.
OP parties.

04. The claimant-respondent 1 herein in order to prove issues 1 and 2 appeared himself as his own witness in the witness box besides one Kapoorji Raina S/o Gopi Nath Raina R/o Kallara Udhampur whereas on the contrary the respondents including appellant herein did not lead any evidence and consequently, the Tribunal passed the impugned award in favour of the claimant-respondent 1 herein.
05. The impugned award is assailed in the instant appeal on the grounds urged therein.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

06. Perusal of the record would reveal that the claimant- respondent 1 herein for proving issues 1 and 2 as has been noticed in the preceding paras appeared as his own witness on 11.10.2014 and deposed that his father was professional religious 'Pandit' and National Insurance Co. 2 used to perform religious ceremonies like ceremonies of Genue, Parbesh, Greh Perbesh, Mundan etc. etc. in Pandit families and would earn monthly income around 15,000/- and in turn would give the said money to him as he was along with his family dependant on the said earnings and he used to earn only 3,000/- to 3,500/- per month being a Teacher in a private school.

sentences.text: Besides proving the fact of dependency upon the deceased, the claimant also proved the date of accident and place of accident where the deceased died as also the cause of death of the deceased being vehicular accident caused by the offending vehicle owned by respondent 2 herein and driven rashly and negligently by respondent 3 herein.

07. Perusal of the record tends to show that the counsel for the claimant-respondent 1 herein though cross-examined the witnesses being the claimant-respondent 1 herein and above named other witness, the counsel for the respondent 1 herein failed to contradict the witnesses or extract anything contrary thereto from them.

The evidence so produced by the claimant-respondent 1 herein before the Tribunal prima facie has been clinching in nature and credible in character having weighed with the Tribunal in drawing satisfaction to award compensation in favour of the claimant-respondent 1 herein in the matter.
08. The Tribunal seemingly has dealt with the claim petition and passed the impugned award rightly and correctly.
However, the accruing of interest shall reckon after the expiry of period of three months from the date of passing of the award.

The award except to the aforesaid extent in the circumstances of the case cannot be found fault with more so in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in case titled as "Anita Sharma and Ors. Vs New India Assurance Co. Ltd. and Anr."
reported in 2021 (1) JKJ (SC) 140 wherein at para 22, following has been observed:
"22.

entities.text: Anita Sharma and Ors. Vs New India Assurance Co. Ltd. and Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Equally, we are concerned over the failure of the High Court to be cognizant of the fact that strict principles of evidence and standards of proof like in a criminal trial are inapplicable in MACT claim cases.
The standard of proof in such like matters is one of the preponderance of probabilities, rather than beyond reasonable doubt.

One needs to be mindful that the approach and role of Courts while examining evidence in accident claim cases ought not to be find fault with non-examination of some best eye witnesses as may happen in a criminal trial; but, instead should be only to analyse the material placed on record by the parties to ascertain whether the claimant's version is more likely than not true."
09.

Viewed, thus, what has been observed, considered and analyzed hereinabove, the appeal fails and is, accordingly, dismissed upholding the impugned award with the aforesaid modification in the date of accrual of interest.
(JAVED IQBAL WANI) JUDGE JAMMU 12.10.2023
